questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner and about to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine while they cross.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait for the person to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the person to cross.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Drink strong coffee.
Wait.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, or showers do not speed this up.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use cruise control near railroad crossings to keep your speed steady.
Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at railroad crossings and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when told to by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Always be careful near railroad tracks.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and work zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. Be extra careful when you see orange signs, cones, or barriers on the road.

questions.question: When must you obey school crossing guards?

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Only if you see children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards near schools. Watch for them and follow their directions.

questions.question: What should you do when a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing?

options.text: Always give them the right-of-way.
Tell them where to cross.
Only give them the right-of-way at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane. They may be blind or partially blind.

questions.question: What is important when turning?

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Speed up.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: Look behind and to both sides of your vehicle before turning. Make sure it is safe to proceed and adjust your speed.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and carefully. Only change lanes when necessary. Each lane change increases accident risk.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When there is a solid line next to your lane.
When there is a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you may cross to change lanes. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only pass when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way.
No passing zone.
One lane ends ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangle sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what headlights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights
Low beam headlights
Four-way flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: If you become tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers
Drink coffee
Open a window

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers
questions.explanation: Stop to rest or let someone else drive. Tiredness slows your reactions and makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: A downward-facing triangle means yield. Slow down and stop if needed. If you stop, do so at the marked line.

questions.question: What can happen if you take prescription drugs while drinking alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect
It will make you more alert
It can make you unfit to drive

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unfit to drive
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Check for vehicles only in the direction you plan to go, then proceed
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first
Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, come to a full stop and check for traffic in all directions before you go.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. The pedestrian is in the middle of the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Proceed if you have the right-of-way
Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane
Wait until the pedestrian crosses before proceeding

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian crosses before proceeding
questions.explanation: At a green light, give the right-of-way to pedestrians in the intersection. Wait until they have fully crossed.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes
You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane
Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating foods high in fat
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to get rid of alcohol. Eating and drinking cannot speed this up.

questions.question: If the roadway is wet or icy, what should you do?

options.text: Reduce your speed
Drive at the posted speed
Speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed
questions.explanation: On wet or icy roads, your tires grip less. Slow down to stay safe.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, when can you safely return to your original lane?

options.text: Beep your horn
See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror
Flash your headlights

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror
questions.explanation: Look for both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. Only then is it safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding or driving too fast for the conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Looking around and focusing on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding or driving too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving above the speed limit or too fast for conditions causes many crashes. Always drive at a safe speed within the legal limit and match the traffic flow.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have left the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the red lights flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and stay stopped while the red lights flash.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. If the bus is on the other side of a divided highway, you do not need to stop.

questions.question: Your tire suddenly blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
Pump the brakes quickly.
Brake hard and steer to the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
questions.explanation: Stay calm during a blowout. Hold the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the gas to let the car slow down. Gently brake when safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed significantly.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Signal before changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal to warn other drivers before moving left or right. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before any lane change.

questions.question: A driving distraction is:

options.text: Anything that makes you take evasive action.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anywhere and anytime. They can cause crashes that result in damage, injury, or death.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn and keep your speed.
Speed up to leave the area quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: You are following a large truck on the freeway. You should:

options.text: Drive closer than you would to a car.
Drive farther back than you would to a car.
Stay to the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive farther back than you would to a car.
questions.explanation: Follow farther behind a large truck than you would a car because trucks have larger blind spots.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing in your lane with no crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before going.
Carefully drive around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in the road, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: You are driving under the influence and cause a crash that kills someone. You may:

options.text: Be charged with vehicular homicide.
Be fined and sent to prison.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Driving under the influence and causing a fatal crash results in a vehicular homicide charge. A conviction can mean a fine and prison time.

questions.question: A good driver should:

options.text: Look straight ahead at their car.
Only focus on the middle of the road.
Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind their car.
questions.explanation: Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind your car. Good drivers know what is happening all around their vehicle at all times.
